newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Malaria sharply up in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Malaria sharply up in S.Africa.

text.p: Heavy summer rains in South Africa have brought a sharp increase in malaria, with health officials reporting 148 people killed by the mosquito-borne disease this year.
Countrywide, doctors recorded 27,604 cases of all types of malaria from the start of the year -- well over the 9,000 cases reported for the whole of 1995.

"It's a very sharp increase," the health department said, warning visitors and communities in the high-risk areas of KwaZulu-Natal, Mpumalanga and Northern provinces to continue taking antimalarial drugs until the end of May.

Officials said the problem was worse this year because of the larger breeding areas for mosquitoes as a result of widespread rain. Large areas are being sprayed in an effort to reduce the size of mosquito populations by December.
Malaria accounts for an estimated 1.5 million deaths a year in Africa, with children making up some 75 percent of fatal cases.
